The branch is the smallest of its blockers: every call first fetches the roster of valid as-of dates (ny_fed_api.py:358-365 hits list_as_of) and builds the URL from the resolved date (_get_endpoints(date=as_of) at :467), which flow.preflight_lookup names; then it REPLACES the caller's as_of with the nearest published date -- get_nearest_date does an abs-difference argmin over the parsed roster at :311-319 and is called at :454-456, with dates[0] at :457-458 when nothing was passed. That selection rule is what nearest_published_date_snap names; flow.preflight_lookup only says the address is not known beforehand. Response-side it also nulls sentinels (Data model empty_strings validator at :283-291 maps three published spellings to None: two literal single quotes, the empty string and the digit 0) and rescales published percents (normalize_percent at :277-281 divides by 100); both validators sit on FederalReserveCentralBankHoldingsData (class at :92, the Fetcher only starts at :294), so these are response rewrites and not query handling. One further mechanism has no canonical at all: query.cusip is comma-joined into a single value at :332-335, which is a list-valued QUERY parameter, whereas path.list_segment names a '+'-joined path segment -- recorded here, folded under the #86 vocabulary debt.

Reads the same H.15 download as TreasuryRates, so the CSV decode and the five-row preamble are NOT its blockers. What is not declarable is the post-request composition: transform_data melts the eleven maturity columns into long (date, maturity, rate) rows (:103), selects each requested date with DatetimeIndex.asof -- nearest published date, not a window or text predicate (:95) -- orders maturity by a Categorical built from a declared roster (:107), rewrites the published 'ND'/'N/A' spellings to null (:100) and divides rate by 100 (:110). A wide declaration of it would be a second model id over rows TreasuryRates already publishes and would not be the oracle's model, so the declaration was retracted this round and the row is recorded NOT_DECLARED. C89 makes the label set carry all five mechanisms the sentence above already named: path.explode (measured present), rows.filter_comparison, rows.order_limit and columns.null_sentinel (all three claim=False in the registry) and columns.rescale (measured absent). Anchoring rescale therefore cannot move this row into shipped cover: three of its five needs stay unclaimed either way.

C94 line re-audit REFUTED multi_request_fanout: this model makes no per-symbol request at all. It repeats ONE URL template with an offset (get_url(date, offset) at latest_financial_reports.py:134-138, count=100&from=offset) and loops while n_hits < total_hits (:161), where total_hits comes from the first response's hits.total.value (:153-154); tickers and CIKs arrive INSIDE each hit (:200-210), they do not select a request. The row is paged (shape get_json_paged, paged=true) and the page count is response-derived, which no spelling names either -- request.body_pagination is about POST bodies. Response-side: lists are COLLAPSED into comma strings (ciks/sics/items joined at :201/:205/:230, symbol/name joined at :215-216) -- the opposite cardinality of path.explode, and display_names is string-split into ticker+name (:207-210); metadata/financial_report are emitted only when the form passes a startswith/in test (:236-248, a conditional derive, and it dereferences report_type without a None guard at :238); items becomes None when empty (:230); rows are deduplicated on the derived url via a seen set (:252-256), which is a distinct-row operation that rows.filter's op set (contains/equals/not_equals/in/prefix) cannot express -- recorded here and under #87 rather than folded onto a present capability. resolve_rows returns the single list at a static pointer (http_json.py:264). Upstream sec module is not vendored in-repo.
